items.title: Missing trial stopping rules

where.quote: All enrolled subjects will receive CMP-001 IT and nivolumab IV according to the treatment schedule until a reason for treatment discontinuation is reached.

why.explanation: The protocol mentions 'until a reason for treatment discontinuation is reached' but does not specify any trial-level stopping rules (e.g., for safety, futility, or efficacy). The M11 template requires a dedicated section on trial stopping rules (4.3), which is missing. This is a critical gap for a phase 2 oncology trial.

fix.suggestion: Add a section on trial stopping rules, including criteria for early termination due to safety (e.g., number of DLTs) or futility (e.g., ORR threshold).

items.title: Missing start and end of trial definitions

where.quote: This is a multicenter, open-label, Phase 2 clinical study of CMP-001 administered by IT injection in combination with intravenous (IV) nivolumab in subjects with unresectable or metastatic melanoma refractory to prior programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade.

why.explanation: The protocol does not define the start of the trial (e.g., date of first subject's first visit) or the end of the trial (e.g., last subject's last visit or database lock). This is required by M11 4.4 and is important for regulatory and operational clarity.

fix.suggestion: Add a statement defining the start of trial (e.g., first subject signed informed consent) and end of trial (e.g., last subject's last protocol-specified assessment or study completion).

items.title: Inconsistent inclusion criterion numbering

where.quote:
5. Able to provide tissue from a core or excisional/incisional biopsy (fine needle aspirate is not sufficient). A fresh tissue biopsy (within 90 days before the start of study treatment) is preferred but an archival sample is acceptable (as a substitute) if no intervening therapy was received. If the Investigator believes it is unsafe to perform a biopsy, the subject may be considered eligible after discussion with the Medical Monitor if tissue and/or prior assessments are available to determine programmed death-ligand 1 expression.
6. NOTE: for tissue sampling details, please refer to the laboratory manual.

why.explanation: The inclusion criteria list has a 'NOTE' as item 6, which is not a criterion but a cross-reference. This disrupts the numbering and could cause confusion when referencing criteria (e.g., 'criterion 6' is not a real criterion).

fix.suggestion: Renumber the criteria so that the NOTE is not numbered as a criterion, or move the NOTE to a separate paragraph.

items.title: Inconsistent definition of 'refractory' in inclusion criteria

where.quote:
Refractory to PD-1 blockade either as monotherapy or in combination with other therapies, as defined by the following criteria:
a. Received treatment with a Food and Drug Administration approved PD-1 blocking antibody for 12 weeks or longer.
b. Have PD (according to RECIST v1.1) within 12 weeks of the last dose of a PD-1 blocking antibody, either as monotherapy or in combination with other agents.

why.explanation: The inclusion criteria require PD within 12 weeks of last dose, but the protocol does not specify whether this is based on BICR or Investigator assessment. Later, the primary endpoint uses BICR, but the inclusion criteria say 'by Investigator assessment' for the confirmatory assessment. This could lead to inconsistency in determining eligibility.

fix.suggestion: Clarify whether the PD for eligibility is based on Investigator or BICR assessment, and ensure consistency with the primary endpoint assessment.

items.title: Contraception section referenced but not provided

where.quote: Women of childbearing potential must have negative serum pregnancy test before dosing at W1D1 and be willing to use an adequate method of contraception (Section 4.3.2.) from the time of consent until at least 150 days after last dose of study treatment.

why.explanation: The protocol references 'Section 4.3.2' for contraception details, but the provided text does not include that section. The M11 template requires a dedicated 'Contraception' section (5.4) which is missing. This leaves the contraception requirements incomplete.

fix.suggestion: Add a detailed contraception section (e.g., M11 5.4) specifying acceptable methods, duration, and male contraception requirements, and update the cross-reference.

items.title: Inconsistent exclusion criterion for prior radiation

where.quote: Received radiation therapy (or other nonsystemic therapy) within 2 weeks before first dose of study treatment on W1D1. Subjects should have recovered (ie, Grade ≤1 or at Baseline) from radiation-related toxicities.

why.explanation: The exclusion criterion says radiation within 2 weeks is exclusionary, but the inclusion criterion 4c requires 'Documented disease progression in any lesion that was previously radiated in order to serve as a target lesion.' This is not necessarily contradictory, but the protocol does not clarify whether a previously radiated lesion that has progressed can be used as a target lesion if radiation was within 2 weeks. The wording could be ambiguous.

fix.suggestion: Clarify that progression in a previously radiated lesion is acceptable even if radiation was within 2 weeks, provided the lesion is not the one being irradiated.

items.title: Missing lifestyle restrictions

where.quote: Treatment with complementary medications (eg, herbal supplements or traditional Chinese medicines) to treat the disease under study within 2 weeks before start of study treatment. Refer to Section 4.4. for prohibited therapies.

why.explanation: The protocol mentions prohibited therapies but does not include a dedicated section on lifestyle restrictions (e.g., alcohol, smoking, diet, sexual activity) as required by M11 5.5. This is a minor gap but could be important for a study with an IT injection and immunotherapy.

fix.suggestion: Add a section on lifestyle restrictions, including any prohibitions on alcohol, smoking, or other activities that could affect safety or PK.

items.title: High burden of vital signs at every visit

where.quote: Vital Signsh

why.explanation: Vital signs are collected at every visit including all weekly visits and Q3W visits, which is excessive and burdensome for patients and staff, especially when many visits are for treatment only.

fix.suggestion: Reduce vital sign frequency to visits where clinically indicated, e.g., only on dosing days or when symptoms occur.

items.title: Adverse Event Monitoring and Concomitant Medications collected at every visit including follow-up

where.quote: Adverse Event Monitoring

why.explanation: AE and concomitant medication monitoring is required at every visit including long-term survival follow-up phone calls, which is impractical and burdensome for sites and patients over years of follow-up.

fix.suggestion: Limit AE and concomitant medication collection to treatment visits and specified follow-up visits, not every LTSFU call.

items.title: Clinical Laboratory Tests at every weekly visit and Q3W visit

where.quote: Clinical Laboratory Tests (hematology, serum chemistry, urinalysis)l

why.explanation: Full lab panel (hematology, chemistry, urinalysis) is required at every weekly visit and every Q3W visit, which is excessive and burdensome for patients, especially those with difficult venous access.

fix.suggestion: Reduce lab frequency to every other week or only when clinically indicated, and consider point-of-care testing.

items.title: Exploratory Biomarker Sampling at multiple visits including W6D2 and W7D1

where.quote: Exploratory Biomarker Sampling

why.explanation: Biomarker sampling is required at W1D1, W5D1, W6D1, W6D2, and W7D1, which is a high frequency of extra blood draws, adding to patient burden and site workload.

fix.suggestion: Consolidate biomarker sampling to fewer timepoints, e.g., only at W1D1 and W7D1, or align with PK sampling.

items.title: Pharmacokinetic Sampling at W6D2 and W7D1 may be hard to collect

where.quote: Pharmacokinetic Sampling

why.explanation: PK sampling on consecutive days (W6D1, W6D2, W7D1) is burdensome and may be difficult for patients to attend, especially if they travel long distances.

fix.suggestion: Reduce PK sampling to a single post-dose timepoint per cycle or use sparse PK sampling.

items.title: Thyroid Function Tests at W3D1 and W7D1 may be unnecessary

where.quote: Thyroid Function Testsl

why.explanation: Thyroid function tests are performed at W3D1 and W7D1 in addition to Q3W visits, which may be excessive given that thyroid abnormalities are typically monitored less frequently.

fix.suggestion: Align thyroid function testing with Q3W visits only, or reduce to every other cycle.

items.title: Tumor Biopsy at W5D1 may be difficult to schedule and invasive

items.title: Primary endpoint ORR may not capture immunotherapeutic response patterns

where.quote: The primary endpoint of the study is the ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed objective response of CR or PR based on RECIST v1.1 as determined by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR).

why.explanation: For immunotherapies, RECIST v1.1 may underestimate responses due to pseudoprogression; iRECIST is often preferred for primary endpoint.

fix.suggestion: Consider using iRECIST or a composite endpoint that includes immune-related response criteria for the primary endpoint.

why.explanation: The safety endpoint is listed but no specific statistical analysis method is described for it in the Statistical Methods section; only general safety assessments are mentioned.

fix.suggestion: Add a detailed analysis description for safety endpoints (e.g., incidence rates, severity grading, relationship) in Section 9.6.

items.title: Inclusion criterion for BRAF V600 mutation status may be overly restrictive

where.quote: Patients with BRAF V600 mutations who refuse a BRAF inhibitor will not be eligible.

why.explanation: This excludes patients who may have contraindications or intolerances to BRAF inhibitors, potentially limiting enrollment and generalizability.

fix.suggestion: Allow enrollment of patients who refuse BRAF inhibitors if they have documented reasons (e.g., contraindication) and discuss with Medical Monitor.

items.title: Inclusion criterion for prior radiation target lesion may be ambiguous

where.quote: Documented disease progression in any lesion that was previously radiated in order to serve as a target lesion.

why.explanation: The wording is unclear: it could mean that a previously radiated lesion must have progressed to be eligible as a target lesion, but it is not specified whether this is required for all target lesions or just one. This ambiguity may lead to inconsistent interpretation and amendments.

fix.suggestion: Clarify that at least one measurable lesion not previously radiated must be present, or specify that previously radiated lesions must have documented progression to be considered measurable.

items.title: Inclusion criterion for tissue biopsy may be impractical and cause enrollment delays

where.quote: A fresh tissue biopsy (within 90 days before the start of study treatment) is preferred but an archival sample is acceptable (as a substitute) if no intervening therapy was received.

why.explanation: Requiring a fresh biopsy within 90 days may be burdensome for patients with refractory melanoma, and the archival sample condition (no intervening therapy) may be difficult to meet, potentially delaying enrollment.

fix.suggestion: Extend the biopsy window or allow archival samples regardless of intervening therapy if adequate tissue is available.

items.title: Exclusion criterion for prior radiation within 2 weeks may be too restrictive for this population

where.quote: Received radiation therapy (or other nonsystemic therapy) within 2 weeks before first dose of study treatment on W1D1.

why.explanation: Patients with refractory melanoma may have had recent palliative radiation; a 2-week washout may be unnecessarily long and could exclude patients who would otherwise benefit.

fix.suggestion: Consider shortening the washout to 1 week or allowing radiation to non-target lesions with recovery to Grade ≤1.

items.title: Exclusion criterion for active autoimmune disease may be too broad

where.quote: Active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in past 2 years; replacement therapy is not considered a form of systemic treatment.

why.explanation: The 2-year window may exclude patients with well-controlled autoimmune conditions (e.g., hypothyroidism on replacement) that are not considered active, but the wording could be misinterpreted. Also, it does not specify which autoimmune diseases are excluded (e.g., vitiligo is often allowed).

fix.suggestion: Specify exceptions for common autoimmune conditions like vitiligo, psoriasis not requiring systemic treatment, and controlled thyroid disease.

items.title: Safety monitoring for adrenal insufficiency is only in a NOTE, not in the Schedule of Activities

where.quote: Subjects previously treated with a CTLA-4–blocking antibody, subjects receiving corticosteroids with daily doses > 5 mg and ≤ 10 mg of prednisone equivalent for > 2 weeks, and subjects with clinical symptoms and/or laboratory findings suggesting risk for adrenal insufficiency should undergo diagnostic tests for adrenal insufficiency via local laboratory.

why.explanation: The protocol mentions diagnostic tests for adrenal insufficiency but does not specify which tests (e.g., cortisol, ACTH) or include them in the Schedule of Activities, which may lead to inconsistent monitoring and missing safety data.

fix.suggestion: Add specific adrenal function tests (e.g., morning cortisol, ACTH stimulation test) to the Schedule of Activities for at-risk patients.

items.title: Exclusion criterion for HIV/HBV/HCV is vague and may cause delays

where.quote: Known or suspected active infection with human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis B virus, or hepatitis C virus (testing is not required unless suspected).

why.explanation: The phrase 'suspected' is subjective and may lead to inconsistent screening practices. Also, not requiring testing may miss asymptomatic infections, which could be a safety concern with immunotherapy.

fix.suggestion: Require routine screening for HIV, HBV, and HCV at baseline, and define 'suspected' more objectively (e.g., based on risk factors or symptoms).
